why: What sits on the substrate. Grain size is a field; these rows hold the laboratory / spacecraft albedos that field lerps between. tag is measured / fitted / invented for the row as a whole.

kinds.label: bare
kinds.why: No cover. The substrate row shows through.

kinds.label: frost
kinds.why: Fresh fine frost is near 0.9; coarsened old ice can drop below 0.4. Grain is the difference between Enceladus and dirty snow.
kinds.cite: Wiscombe and Warren 1980; Warren 1982 snow albedo

kinds.label: dust
kinds.why: Settled lofted dust. Mars-coloured; not a dust budget.
kinds.cite: Wolff et al. Mars dust optical properties, fitted to 0.25

kinds.label: lag
kinds.why: Involatile residue left when frost retreats. Darkens the cell until new frost buries it.
kinds.cite: Cometary lag crust analogue; albedo invented

kinds.label: tholin
kinds.why: Photochemical goo. Titan dunes, Pluto Cthulhu, Iapetus Cassini Regio.
kinds.cite: Cruikshank et al. tholin optical constants; geometric albedo ~0.05

kinds.label: sulfur
kinds.why: Io's yellow. Overlay rgb shifts with cell T (allotropes); the photograph globe stays kind-keyed.
kinds.cite: Nash and Fanale 1977 sulfur allotropes on Io

kinds.label: evaporite
kinds.why: Ceres Occator bright spots are sodium carbonate. A bright salt with a subsurface source.
kinds.cite: De Sanctis et al. 2016 Occator carbonates

kinds.label: regolith
kinds.why: Gardened airless soil. Space weathering darkens it with cell age.

kinds.label: ejecta
kinds.why: Fresh crater rays are bright fines on top of the surface. They fade by space weathering, not by topography.
kinds.cite: Lunar ray albedo; fade is fitted

kinds.label: microbial mat
kinds.why: Pigmented cover before plants. Two billion years of Earth looked like this; non-Whittaker worlds with life use it.
kinds.cite: invented; no Solar System analogue on the globe

kinds.label: vegetation
kinds.why: Whittaker plant cover. One case of the general cover model, not a separate engine.
